@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+experiment_id: e0b-browsergym-base-llama3_2-1b
+description: "E0 on a second lineage: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, untrained, through the identical two eval splits, seeds and per-turn budget as e0. Byte-for-byte a copy of e0-browsergym-base-qwen3-1_7b with the model slug swapped, so the two differ in exactly one thing. It answers whether the reward-shaping effects the study reports are properties of the reward or of Qwen3, which is a question the reviewer will ask and which no amount of seed replication inside one lineage can settle. Read the numbers against e0, not against e27 - this is a base-model reference, not a trained condition. Two caveats belong in any writeup that cites it. Llama-3.2 has no thinking mode, so `content` carries the whole generation and there is no reasoning trace for a length reward to compress; a Llama arm therefore asks whether the length reward does anything absent a think block, which is a related question rather than a pure lineage replicate. And 1B against 1.7B is the closest size match available in this family, not an equal one. Llama is not a preference here but the only option: TRL matches chat templates by exact string equality and refuses to train on anything outside its fixed list, of which the Llama 3.x pair are the only non-Qwen entries that fit the card. Run with `python -m eval.runner --config <this> --base-model`."
+seed: 42
+
+model:
+  slug: llama3.2-1b
+  lora_r: 16
+  max_seq_length: 8192
+  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.30
+
+training:
+  # Present for the env geometry only; nothing trains here. Copied from e0 so
+  # the two base-model evals differ in exactly one thing, the model.
+  mode: agentic
+  env: browsergym
+  env_config:
+    benchmark: miniwob
+    tasks: [click-menu-2, click-dialog-2]
+    # Must be up before launch and does not survive a box restart:

+    miniwob_url: http://localhost:8080/miniwob/
+    max_turns: 8
+  env_server:
+    repo_path: /workspace/OpenEnv/envs
+    port: 8000
+  max_prompt_length: 4096
+
+rewards:
+  compose_method: naive_sum
+  env_reward:
+    enabled: true
+    weight: 1.0
+
+eval:
+  temperature: 0.0
+  do_sample: false
+  # Pinned to e0's value, which is pinned to e27's. Llama will almost certainly
+  # generate far shorter completions than Qwen3 for want of a think block; that
+  # is a result to measure, not a reason to move the budget.
+  max_new_tokens: 4096
+  agentic:
+    splits:
+      - name: held_out
+        n_episodes: 100
+      - name: shifted
+        n_episodes: 100
+        env_config:
+          tasks: [navigate-tree, click-checkboxes-transfer]
+        seed_offset: 200000

content.text: Based on my review, I've traced the new model registry entry through its consumers (`pipeline/training/grpo_runner.py` and `pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py`). The registry addition points to a third-party HuggingFace mirror (`unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`), and the callers invoke `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_cfg["model_name"], ...)` with no `revision=` pin and no hash verification. The comment in `registry.py` claims a one-time chat-template hash check was done, but nothing in the code enforces this — the model is refetched from HF hub on every load, and any subsequent change to the mirror (or maintainer-account compromise) will silently propagate to the shared GPU box (memory context notes the box is multi-user). The YAML config is pure data; the test file's allowlist is not a security surface itself but does codify that the pipeline permits an unpinned mirror.

findings.explanation: This entry pins a third-party HuggingFace mirror by name only. The callers that consume it (`pipeline/training/grpo_runner.py` L46-52 and `pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py` L392-397) call `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_cfg["model_name"])` / `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_cfg["model_name"], ...)` with no `revision=` argument, so every load resolves `main` on the mirror at fetch time. The registry comment attests that the chat_template hashes byte-identical to TRL's stock template (sha256 5816fce10444e03c) and that the only diffs are benign — but that verification lives in a comment, not in code. If the mirror maintainer's account is compromised, or the mirror pushes a new revision, the pipeline picks it up silently on next fetch: (a) a modified `chat_template` or `tokenizer_config.json` would be the exact confound the comment worries about (silently altering the tool-call format and invalidating the cross-lineage comparison this experiment exists to make); (b) a `.bin` (pickle-format) checkpoint substituted for the current safetensors would execute arbitrary code in `torch.load` during `from_pretrained` — `trust_remote_code` is unset (good) but pickle deserialization is a separate RCE vector that HF's automatic scanning is best-effort, not guaranteed. Per project memory, the GPU box is shared with another user, so a compromised load has cross-tenant impact. The test-time `ALLOWED_MIRRORS` guard only asserts the name string; it does nothing to bind the fetched artifact to the state that was manually verified.

Optionally add `use_safetensors=True` to hard-refuse pickle checkpoints. That makes the byte-identity claim in the comment a code-enforced invariant rather than a one-off manual check.
